subject.title: Multi-profile profile targeting/config truth is ambiguous with ~/.openclaw-* homes on macOS

question: What should the macOS profile-targeting contract be when an explicit root `--profile` conflicts with inherited LaunchAgent identity, profile-name casing, or separate `.openclaw-*` homes?
rationale: Source inspection confirms a stale-label subcase, but deciding whether explicit profiles override managed labels, how casing resolves, and which mixed-home layouts are supported changes the operator contract and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Make explicit profile authoritative
options.body: Treat root `--profile` as the selected config/state/service target, clear only stale OpenClaw-managed launchd labels, preserve intentional custom labels, and add clearer status output plus live macOS proof.

options.title: Preserve label override precedence
options.body: Keep `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL` stronger than `--profile` and document nested cross-profile lifecycle commands as unsupported unless the operator clears service identity manually.

options.title: Defer to broader profile design
options.body: Keep this issue as a design umbrella until maintainers decide casing, mixed-home, service-label, and status truth together.

recommendation.title: Make explicit profile authoritative
recommendation.body: Treat root `--profile` as the selected config/state/service target, clear only stale OpenClaw-managed launchd labels, preserve intentional custom labels, and add clearer status output plus live macOS proof.
